content.title: About
content.content: Beef Stroganoff is a classic Russian dish consisting of thinly sliced beef fillet sautéed and simmered in a creamy tomato‑based sauce with onions and mushrooms. It is traditionally served with mashed potatoes, rice, or egg noodles.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is named after Count Stroganov, though its exact origin is uncertain.
The first known recipe appeared in the early 19th‑century cookbook “Culinary Recipes” by French chef Pierre Culin.
During the Soviet era, Stroganoff was often made with pork, chicken, or even fish in different regions.
The sauce is commonly made with sour cream in Russia, while Western versions use heavy cream or tomato paste.
Beef Stroganoff has become popular worldwide and is featured on many restaurant menus.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef supplies iron, which is vital for hemoglobin formation and energy production.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish offers vitamin B12 and niacin, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Cream or sour cream adds calcium and phosphorus, supporting bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants from mushrooms
items.content: Mushrooms are rich in selenium and polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Traditional recipes use cream or sour cream, making the dish calorie‑dense and high in saturated fats.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Adding soy sauce or prepared broth can increase sodium, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy should use dairy‑free alternatives.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity to red meat
items.content: Those with a sensitive stomach may prefer lean cuts or substitute beef with chicken.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Slice beef into thin strips and quickly sear over high heat, then set aside. In the same pan sauté onions and mushrooms, add tomato paste, sour cream (or cream) and a splash of beef broth. Return the meat, heat through 5‑7 minutes without overcooking. Serve with mashed potatoes, rice or egg noodles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked Beef Stroganoff in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat gently with a little broth or cream to keep the sauce from drying out.
